info.name: Video Gallery
info.summary: Every video in your account, in one cinematic library that plays any format
Toate videoclipurile din contul tău, într-o bibliotecă cinematografică ce redă orice format
info.description:
Video Gallery collects every video file in your account into a single library, arranged by the date each one was taken, and plays all of them in the browser — including the formats a browser cannot open on its own.
* A timeline built from real capture dates, read from the file's own metadata, not just its modification time * Rows of large cover cards; move the pointer over one and it starts playing a short silent preview in place * Direct play whenever the browser can handle the file, so the original quality is streamed untouched * Hardware transcoding for everything else — HEVC, 10-bit, VC-1, MPEG-2, DTS, TrueHD, AVI, MKV — turned into a stream the browser plays with ordinary controls, using the GPU * Only the parts that need changing are converted: a file with an unsupported audio track keeps its video as is * Seeking restarts the conversion at the requested moment, so jumping ahead in a long film stays quick * Subtitle tracks embedded in the file are offered in the player, alongside every audio track * "Open in external player" hands the untouched original to VLC, Infuse or any player on the device * Resume where you left off, across devices * Share a video or a folder with a person, a group, or anyone holding a link, and decide for each whether the file may be downloaded as well as watched * A folder of numbered files is recognised as a series, and the next part is offered when one finishes * Folders are sorted into kinds — courses, camera, series, films — by rules the administrator writes, and each kind is shown the way it wants showing: a course opened at the part worth watching next, a folder of clips newest first * Temporary files live wherever the administrator points them — a fast disk away from the system drive — and every one of them is accounted for and removed
info.author: Cristian Casapu
